defs.example: I have seen things that lead me to believe that real evil exists.

defs.text: A professor is a teacher at a college or university.

defs.example: Everyone joked about how bad his tennis was.

defs.text: A doubt is a question or uncertainty about something.

defs.text: If you doubt someone or something, you do not believe them completely.

defs.text: A moon is a thing like a small planet that goes around another planet.
defs.example: Galileo saw four moons of Jupiter: Callisto, Europa, Ganymede and Io.

defs.text: An address is the location where a building is or where a person lives.
If you address a person, you refer to them using a name or title.
defs.example: You will address me as Sir from now on.

defs.text: If you address a group, you talk in front of it.
defs.example: The Prime Minister will address the United Nations.

defs.text: If you address a letter, you write an address on it.
defs.example: She addressed the envelope to "Mr. John Black."

defs.text: A noun used in English.
defs.example: This is an example with ow.

defs.text: A match is a game of football, tennis, etc.
defs.example: We lost the first match, but hope to win our next two.

defs.text: A match is something that goes with something else because they are similar.
defs.example: I can't find a match for this sock.

defs.text: A match is a small stick that has a chemical on one end of it. You use it to make a fire.
defs.example: He lit a match for some light in the dark room.

defs.text: A match is a situation in which two things go together well.
If two things match, they go together because they are similar in some way.
defs.example: Look around for a table you like or one which most closely matches your room.

defs.text: If you are matched against someone, you are their opponent in a competition.
If you are nervous, you are tense and worried about something.
defs.example: I am nervous about my examinations.

defs.text: Related to the nerves.
defs.example: Nervous system.

defs.text: When you choose a thing, you decide you want it and not something else.
defs.example: The manager and coaches will choose the starting line-up.

defs.text: If you decide something, there were different things you could do, but you choose one.
defs.example: The government has decided to cut spending.

defs.text: The press are the people and organisations that report the news.
defs.example: The president gave an interview with members of the press.

defs.text: The press is the news as it is reported.
defs.example: The next day, the fire was all over the press.

defs.text: A press is a company that prints books.
defs.example: The book was published by University of California Press.

defs.text: A press is a machine that prints books, newspapers, etc.
defs.example: Stop the presses! We've got a new story.

defs.text: If you press something, you push it against something.
defs.example: She pressed her nose against the window.

defs.text: If you press clothes, you use an iron to make them flat.
If you press someone to do something, you ask them strongly or many times.
defs.example: When she pressed him for an answer, he hung up the phone.

defs.text: If you press on or forward, you keep going even though it's difficult.
A small trouble or problem.
defs.example: I can do it – no bother.

defs.text: A bother is somebody or something that makes trouble for you.
defs.example: I don't want to be a bother, so I'll just go out by myself.

defs.text: If you bother to do something, you make an effort to do it.
defs.example: Don't bother with the dishes. I'll do them later.

defs.text: If something bothers someone, it disturbs or them.
defs.example: Would it bother you if I smoked?

defs.text: The lowest part of the leg, below the ankle; the part of the body used to stand on.
defs.example: He hurt his foot playing football.

defs.text: The bottom or base of something.
defs.example: We meet at the foot of the hill.

defs.text: A length of 12 inches; three feet is almost one meter. The foot is used mostly in the United States, but was common in Europe a long time ago.
defs.example: There are about 30 centimeters in one foot.

defs.text: The blame for something bad is the idea that you made or let it happen.
defs.example: You keep your mouth shut and I'll take the blame.

defs.text: If you blame someone or something for something bad, you say or think that they are the reason for or cause of it.
defs.example: It's not your fault... don't blame yourself.

defs.text: A type is one thing or a group of things that are all members of a larger group because of some similarity.
defs.example: I use the same type of camera at work.

defs.text: A type is a person who is like people from a particular group who are all similar in some way.
defs.example: He's not the usually football type.

defs.text: Type is letters that have been printed by a machine.
defs.example: The type in this book is too small to read.

defs.text: Type is the blocks of metal with raised letters used to print text.
defs.example: With Gutenberg's movable type printing, books could be made using less money.

defs.text: If you type something, you write it using a keyboard.
defs.example: I typed up the letter very quickly, so I hope there are no mistakes.

defs.text: If you type something, you put it into a particular group because of some group similarity.
defs.example: The Red Cross collects the blood and the technicians in the hospitals cross and type it.

defs.text: A mission is a quest given by someone to gain something.
defs.example: The Interpol is on a mission to find the international terrorists.

defs.text: In some religions and myths, heaven is a place where you may go after you die. Heaven is usually seen as a happy place where good people are rewarded.
defs.example: I miss my grandmother, but I know she's with God in heaven.

defs.text: The sky.
The skies or places in outer space.
defs.example: I looked up to the heavens in delight.

defs.text: Much happiness, or a cause of much happiness.
defs.example: He's been in heaven ever since we told him.

defs.text: A race is when people compete to see who is the fastest at either driving or running.
defs.example: There was a race to see who could finish first.

defs.text: A race is a group of people that come from the same place and have similar traditions.
A race is a group of people with the same physical characteristics, such as skin color, hair color and type, etc.
defs.example: There were three different races at the school; s, s, and Asians

defs.text: When a person races, he competes with other people to see who can go the fastest.
defs.example: Tom was hungry, so he raced George down to the ice cream truck.

defs.text: A risk is something bad that could possibly happen.
defs.example: There are many risks associated with the stock market.

defs.text: A risk is the chance of something bad happening.
defs.example: The risk of us failing is too great.

defs.text: To risk something means to take a chance with something.
defs.example: She risked hypothermia by swimming the English Channel.

defs.text: An action is something that you do, or something that happens, especially with motion.

defs.text: Smoke is the gray or black substance that goes up into the air when something burns.
defs.example: The smoke from that factory is making me sick.

defs.text: A cigarette.
A light grey colour tinted with blue.
If somebody is smoking, they are in smoke, usually from a cigarette.
defs.example: Excuse me, you can't smoke in the restaurant.

defs.text: If something is smoking, it is making smoke.
defs.example: The fire's still smoking. You'd better put some more water on it.

defs.text: Some help.

defs.text: When you notice something

defs.text: A notice is a piece of paper with information or a warning.
defs.example: She sent us a notice about the change of dates.

defs.text: Notice is information that you give to someone.
defs.example: The shop closed without any notice.

defs.text: If you notice something, you become aware of it.
defs.example: You didn't even notice that I cut my hair.

defs.text: The act of smiling; the form of one's mouth when one is smiling.
defs.example: A visit to the fair always brings a smile to my face.

defs.text: To put one's mouth in a form which shows that one is happy; to have the sides of one's mouth higher than the middle.
defs.example: She smiled at me. I think she likes me!

defs.text: A director is a person who is in charge of something.
defs.example: The film director was doing a very good job.

defs.text: A guard is a person or a group of people who watch something and try to stop anything bad from happening to it.
defs.example: After leaving the police he worked as a security guard at an airport.

defs.text: A guard is something that is a barrier between you and something dangerous.
defs.example: You push a button and a guard comes down to keep your hands out of the machine while it works.

defs.text: A guard is a position on a basketball team who moves the ball to help their team gain points
A guard is an offensive position in American football who plays either side of the center.
If you guard something, you watch it and try to stop anything bad from happening to it.
defs.example: The front gate was guarded by Iraqi soldiers.

defs.text: When you begin something, you start to do the first part of a longer action.
defs.example: A journey always begins with a first step.

defs.text: A spot is a small area that's different from that area around it.
defs.example: I have a bald spot on my head.

defs.text: A spot is a place, position, or period of time.
defs.example: "There... " I said, pointing to a spot near Forest Hills.

defs.text: A spot is a place, especially one that you like going to.
defs.example: Pizza and seared halibut are among the excellent dishes at this Wine Country hot spot.

defs.text: A spot is a place in a group.
defs.example: A 42-35 victory that gave the Spartans a playoff spot.

defs.text: If you spot something, you see it, even though it may be difficult to see.
defs.example: I spotted Lisa shopping at the grocery store with Mike yesterday.

defs.text: If something is spotted, it has or gets spots on it.
defs.example: Oh no! That red wine spotted my new shirt!

defs.text: If you spot someone money, you give or lend it to them.
defs.example: Can you spot me a five for the burger?

defs.text: If you spot someone points in a game, you let them have points to make the game more even.
If you are surprised, something that you didn't expect happened.
If you are innocent you do not know evil.
defs.example: How could he hurt an innocent child?!?

defs.text: If you are innocent of a crime you did not do that crime.
defs.example: I swore to the police that I was innocent.

defs.text: A narrator is someone who narrates or tells stories.
If someone is your enemy that person is against you, or does not like you.
defs.example: I have no enemies that I know of.

defs.text: In war the enemy is the country or army that is attacking your country or army.
defs.example: He was sent to jail because he was working for the enemy.

defs.text: A battle is when different groups or teams fight each other.
A battle is a personal challenge or struggle.
defs.example: After a long battle with cancer, he finally returned to work.

defs.text: If you allow something, you let it happen; you say it's OK.

defs.text: A department is a part of a business, school, hospital or other institution that has a particular job.

defs.text: A department is a part of a large store, which sells one kind of product.
defs.example: You can find balls in the sporting goods department.

defs.text: Somebody's department is the things that they are good at or responsible for.
defs.example: Sorry, I can't help you. That's not my department.

If you feel guilty you feel bad about something you did.

defs.text: A suit is a set of clothes that includes a coat or and pants or dress.
defs.example: Everyone wears a suit where I work.

defs.text: A suit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.
defs.example: The law suit was for one million dollars.

defs.text: A suit is a set in a pack of cards, such as the spades, hearts, diamonds or clubs.
If something suits you it fits you; that is, it is right for you or good for you.

defs.text: A hero is a person who is very brave and does great things. The hero may be real or not real, and often defeats dangerous of the people.
defs.example: The hero Hercules was said to have killed the nine head snake called "hydra."

defs.text: Your hero is a person you greatly admire. This may also be someone you want to be similar to.
defs.example: Leonardo DaVinci used to be my hero.

defs.text: Your hero is someone who saves or defends you.
defs.example: "Oh, my hero!" she said to her rescuer.

defs.text: A hero is the main character in a story or film (movie).
defs.example: A female hero is a heroine.

defs.text: If a person destroys something, they break it or make it not exist anymore.
defs.example: The house was destroyed by the bomb.

defs.text: If someone destroys a person, they hurt that person badly or cause that person much trouble.
defs.example: Mary was destroyed by her failiure to get into college.

defs.example: We had to try a bunch of times before we could start the car.

defs.text: A bunch can also mean a group or cluster.
defs.example: Grapes come in bunches.

defs.text: A chicken is a bird that farmers raise for meat and eggs.
defs.example: My father went out back, caught a chicken, cut off its head, and cleaned it for dinner.

defs.text: Chicken is the meat of a chicken.
defs.example: They make a very tasty fried chicken dish here that comes with vegetables and potatoes.

defs.text: If cost, value, amount, sound, temperature, etc. is low, it is small.

defs.text: If you are admitted to an institution, the institution starts taking care of you.
defs.example: He was admitted to hospital and he is having his operation next week.

defs.text: If you admit something, you say reluctantly that it is true.
defs.example: She admitted that she robbed the bank.

defs.text: If you cross something, you go from one side of it to the other side.
defs.example: Don't cross the street until the light turns green.

defs.text: If you cross something, you put one part over another perpendicularly.
defs.example: She crossed her ankles: she put one foot on the other side of the other foot.

defs.text: If you cross someone, you do something that the person does not like.
defs.example: Don't cross me. Make sure to agree with me.

defs.text: If you cross, you go in a path that will intersect with someone else's path.
defs.example: Boats crossing from starboard have right-of-way.

defs.text: When kings and other royalty have favorites, these are people they trust.
defs.example: He was a favorite of the king.

defs.text: Taste is the sense linked to the tongue, usually when eating food. The taste is how people can enjoy their food.
defs.example: The main tastes are sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

defs.text: Someone's taste, is the kind of food, books, clothing, etc. that they like.
defs.example: She has great taste in clothes, but I don't understand her taste in men.

defs.text: The way something tastes is the sense you get when you put it in your mouth.

defs.text: If you taste something, you put it in your mouth to see if you like it.
defs.example: Here, taste this soup and tell me if it needs more salt.

defs.text: A prince is the son of the king and queen in a country, and brother of the princess. The prince can also be the husband of a princess.
defs.example: Our great-great-great-great-grandfather is a prince.

defs.text: If you form something, you give it shape or structure.

defs.text: If something is silly, it's not important or serious.
defs.example: I was making silly little jokes and she was laughing.

defs.text: If you are silly, you don't think about things carefully or you are not serious.
defs.example: Sometimes it's hard to believe how silly students can be.

defs.text: If you mention something, you say it or talk about it, but only very briefly.
defs.example: Father Poole became very excited when I mentioned your name.

defs.text: If you build something, you make it out of pieces of other things.
defs.example: I built the house with wood and stone.

defs.text: If you build something, you make it bigger, stronger, or better.
defs.example: This is a new idea that others can build upon.

defs.text: Your throat is a tube inside your neck. It takes air from your mouth to your lungs.
defs.example: My throat hurts from singing too much.

defs.text: A hole is an empty space in an object or material.
defs.example: He fell into the water through a hole in the ice.

defs.text: A track is a line on the ground or in space that people, animals or vehicles follow.
defs.example: It's right where Hardy Road crosses the railroad tracks.

defs.text: A track is a single part of an audio recording that can be separated from other parts of a recording.
defs.example: You can make digital copies of the CD tracks and save them in MP3 format.

defs.text: A track is a mark left on the ground by somebody or something walking or driving.
defs.example: Phillip glanced at the policemen measuring and marking the tire tracks.

defs.text: If you keep track of something, you follow it or always know where it is or what's happening with it.
defs.example: I use a watch in order to keep track of how long I've been studying.

defs.text: If you track something down, you find it after looking for it.
defs.example: He was trying to track down where she lived.

defs.text: If you track something, you follow it, to see where it's going or how it's changing.

defs.example: The kids tracked mud all over my clean floors.

defs.example: Remember to lock the door when you leave the house.

defs.text: Breakfast is the first meal that we eat in the morning.

defs.text: An engine is the part of a machine which gives it power.

defs.example: Video games are addictive because they are so fun that you want to try it again so many times.

defs.text: In science, pressure is force applied over an area.

defs.text: A gentleman is a man that treats other nicely, or a man of higher class.
To call someone a gentleman is also a polite way to talk to someone.
defs.example: Please come with me, gentlemen.

defs.text: If you introduce someone or something, you make them known to someone else.
defs.example: Let me introduce you to my friend.

defs.text: Fate is a power that decides what will happen to us in the future.
having been divided; having the unity destroyed
defs.example: Congress...gave the impression of...a confusing sum of disconnected local forces

defs.text: (especially of wood) cut or ripped longitudinally with the grain
defs.example: we bought split logs for the fireplace

defs.text: A split between two groups is a strong disagreement.
defs.example: Time brought about the split between Moscow and Beijing.

defs.text: A split in something, is a place where it breaks into two or where there is a long thing opening.
defs.example: The split in the wood had grown wider over the years.

defs.text: If you do the splits, you spread your legs so that your feet are pointing away from each other.
A kind of ice cream dessert.
If a group of people splits or is split, the people don't agree, so the group becomes more than one group.
defs.example: Female voters overall are evenly split between Obama (48%) and McCain (47%).

defs.text: If you split something, you separate, cut, or break it into different parts.
defs.example: East and West Germany were split apart at the end of World War II.

defs.text: If you split your skin, you cut it by hitting it.
If you split, you leave.
Something that happened recently happened shortly before now.
If something is expected to happen, it is regarded as likely to happen and can be anticipated.
defs.example: The expected storm never arrived.

defs.text: If you add x to y, you put x and y together.
defs.example: Cook for five minutes, then add the remaining spices to the soup.

defs.text: If you add time, or price, you increase it.
defs.example: A new kitchen would add value to the home.

defs.text: If you add something to what you've said, you say something more.
defs.example: I paused for a moment, then added, "Would you mind if I had some pudding?"

defs.text: When something moves slowly or does something slowly, it takes a very long time to do it.
defs.example: She was very tired, and walked slowly up the stairs to bed.

defs.text: An alarm is a signal that something needs attention or a machine that makes the signal.
defs.example: I wake up, without an alarm clock, at seven or eight a.m.

defs.text: Alarm is a feeling of worry or fear.
defs.example: They watched with some alarm as the speeding car got closer.

defs.text: If you alarm someone, you make them feel worried or scared.
defs.example: The school was alarmed by the number of children failing math.

defs.text: A member is someone belonging to a group or organization.
defs.example: I am a member of Simple English Wikipedia.

defs.text: To enter is to go into something.
defs.example: I entered the building through the side door.

defs.text: To enter is to go in.
defs.example: Please pay the fare before you enter.

defs.text: To type something into a computer.
defs.example: I entered all the necessary information but it still won't work.

defs.text: A garden is a place where flowers and other plants grow where people want them to. Frequently it is a small place with a wall around it, near a house. It may have rocks and other things in it to look beautiful.
defs.example: She spends a lot of time taking care of the flowers in her garden.

defs.text: If you are brave, fear will not stop you.
defs.example: You must be very brave to run into a burning house.

defs.text: A pig is a mammal.
defs.example: On this farm, we have over 200 pigs, but no cows or horses.

defs.text: If you call someone a pig you mean that they eat too much, are not clean, or are not a nice person.
defs.example: My sister is such a pig. We bought a bag of sweets and she ate them all in one day.

defs.text: worthy of imitation
defs.example: exemplary behavior

defs.text: A model is a something that is made to look or act like something else, usually being smaller or simpler than the original.
defs.example: Mathematical models can greatly help researchers understand the behavior of real systems.

defs.text: A model is an example of something, a goal, or a way to do something.
defs.example: Both men and women who had public athletic role models during childhood were more likely to play sports at a higher level.

defs.text: A model is a person who puts on clothes, glasses, jewelery, etc. to show them at shows and in photographs or who poses for paintings or sculptures.
defs.example: High-fashion runway models are typically 5 foot 10 inches or taller.

defs.text: A model is a kind or design of car or other machine.
defs.example: The wireless phone will be installed in future models from GM, Toyota and Honda.

defs.text: If you model clothes, jewelery, etc., you wear them to show them at shows and in photographs.
If you model an action, you show how it is done.
defs.example: Parents should model the behavior they want without forcing or controlling the child.

defs.text: If you model x on y, you try to make x like y.
defs.example: There's a youth baseball field modeled after Fenway Park in the old Memorial Stadium.

defs.text: If you model something, you make a smaller, simpler copy of it.
defs.example: He's trying to model the human thought process on the computer.

defs.text: A finger is a long thin part of your hand that bends. Most people have four fingers and one thumb on each hand.
defs.example: He only uses one finger on the keyboard.

defs.text: Medicine is something you put into or on your body when you are sick to make yourself healthy.
defs.example: After I got out of the hospital, I went to the drug store and bought medicine for my ear problem.

defs.text: Medicine is the science of health care.
defs.example: The school of medicine at the University of Western Ontario has produced some of the country's best doctors.

defs.text: If you have access to something, you can use it, look at it, enter it, etc.
defs.example: As a student, you have access to all our facilities including the library and computers.

defs.text: If you access something, you get information from it, usually using a computer.
defs.example: The product enables multiple systems to access a single database.

defs.text: If something is flat, it has a surface with no high places or low places.
defs.example: There are a lot of mountains, and very little flat land for farming.

defs.text: with flat sails
defs.example: sail flat against the wind

defs.text: in a forthright manner; candidly or frankly
defs.example: he didn't answer directly

defs.text: A flat is a rented room or rooms in a building with other flats.
defs.example: Would you like to come back to my flat and watch TV?

defs.text: A flat makes a note one semitone lower than a natural: it is shown by the symbol ♭.
If you do something easily, you have no trouble doing it.
defs.example: They won the game easily, 6–0.

defs.text: If something could easily happen, it is likely.
A screw is a small metal thing for holding pieces of wood together. You turn it to move it in or out of the wood.
defs.example: I need some screws to hold the shelf to the wall.

defs.text: If you screw in a screw, you put it into a piece of wood by turning it.
defs.example: I screwed the hinge into the door.

defs.text: If you say, "screw this", you decide not to do it because you are frustrated.
defs.example: Screw this, I will just sit here and do nothing all day.

defs.text: If you screw someone, you have sex with them.
If you are insane you can not think well because of mental illness.
defs.example: He was sent to a mental hospital because he was insane.

defs.text: An insane idea is very strange, like something a crazy person might think of.
defs.example: That has got to be the most insane thing I have ever heard.

defs.text: If something is insane it does not make sense. It is strange in a bad way.
defs.example: The price of gas these days is insane.

defs.text: The weather in a place is the air temperature, the number of clouds, and the amount of wind and rain or snow.
defs.example: The weather conditions at the airport are bad. I don't think the plane will be able to fly.

defs.text: A path is a way to get to a place. It is like a small road, often made of dirt.
defs.example: That path leads into the woods.

defs.text: A path is the way something moves.
defs.example: The planets follow an elliptical path.

defs.text: A soft thing is nice to touch.
defs.example: cotton is a soft cloth.

defs.text: Something that is soft is flexible.
defs.example: When metal is heated it gets soft.

defs.text: A soft drink is a beverage that is carbonated, does not contain alcohol, and is sweet.
Broadly, the term soft drinks can refer to any drinks that do not contain alcohol.
To harm someone or an animal means to hurt someone or an animal; to injure someone or an animal.
defs.example: In the attack, he caused her serious bodily harm.

defs.text: To harm something means to damage something.
